analysis.title: JPM | US Energy: Median Power Stock -50%, Hormuz Attacks Rise, Russian Refinery Strikes, Nuclear Proposal, Polish Gold Buying, Renewables Buildout Accelerates, DVN, EOG, AEE Recaps
key_insights: The Nasdaq shed $2.5 trillion in market cap on Thursday 11/5, the largest single-day drop on record. JPM's BTM, Nuclear and IPP baskets have lost about $550bn, $160bn and $90bn in market cap from their peaks. The median drawdown from the 52-week high across the underlying names is 50%, and plenty of names are down 70-90%.
Over the past month the BTM basket is down 30%, the nuclear basket is down 25% and IPPs are down 22%.

Delta-one flow notes: CTAs likely turned net short US equities after the sell-off broke several momentum signals. Net selling in S&P 500 futures was about $11Bn in the first ~1.5 hours of cash trading.

Volatility-targeting portfolios have an estimated ~$50Bn of equity exposure to sell over the next few days as target leverage falls from about the 67th to the 30th percentile. Levered ETFs sold more than $60Bn of equity exposure into the close, about 90% of it tech.

Iran reported three more tanker incidents on November 5, at least five since Sunday versus 35 across October. Tehran said two tankers struck mines and one caught fire. Causes and supply losses are unverified.
Ukrainian drones reportedly struck the industrial area housing Russia's 340 kb/d Ryazan refinery in an attack involving more than 200 drones. Refinery damage and lost throughput are unconfirmed.

Iran sent a nuclear proposal to Washington via Qatar. It conditions substantive talks and a Hormuz reopening on seven demands, including sanctions relief, unfrozen assets and reparations. Washington is reviewing it and no agreement exists.

JPM's Center for Geopolitics sees US escalation options (a repeat of spring strikes, attacks on energy and civilian infrastructure, or a strike on a nuclear target), all of which risk Iranian retaliation. It sees a narrower Strait-focused arrangement as the best near-term outcome.

Poland's central bank reached its 700-tonne gold target after buying an estimated 27 tonnes in October. Gold was 31% of reserves at end-September and Governor Glapinski left the door open to more purchases.

The IEA forecasts 4,800 GW of renewable additions in 2026-31, about 60% more than the prior six years. Solar is over 75% of additions. China's share falls from over 60% in 2025 to an average of 53%, and India becomes the second-largest growth market.

Of 41 data-center ballot measures this week, all but one went against data centers (Ballotpedia). Google still plans a $17bn Wyoming data center powered partly by a 702 MW fuel-cell project with carbon capture.

Trump-backed critical minerals financing deals (equity stakes, warrants) face more scrutiny after the Democratic midterm sweep. USA Rare Earth, Vulcan Elements and Kaz Resources were singled out earlier this year.

DVN's portfolio review ended with no incremental asset sales beyond the $4.2bn Eagle Ford sale to Crescent. JPM expects a modestly negative stock reaction. DVN is committed to $1bn of 4Q26 buybacks and a faster pace in 2027 after the January 2027 close.

EOG's 3Q26 print was slightly ahead of JPM and Street estimates. It raised its base dividend 8% to $4.40 annualized (2.8% yield) and expects $9.7bn of 2026 FCF versus JPM's $8.9bn. JPM expects a neutral reaction.
COP beat on 3Q26 EPS, raised its dividend 11% to $0.93 per quarter and guided to lower 2027 capex. JPM expects a slightly positive reaction.
HMH was downgraded to Neutral from Overweight after a 3Q26 miss and a push-out of equipment awards and rig reactivations into 2027.
Tenaris guided 4Q26 implied EBITDA of $853mm, about 12.7% above JPM and 13.2% above the Street. JPM raised 2027E EBITDA by 11.6%. The shares rose 1.1% on a day when energy fell.

JPM prefers downstream and integrated models over upstream Canadian producers because it sees a tighter product market and wider crude differentials. It stays Neutral on CNQ (C$75 target) and Overweight on CVE (C$56 target).

Utilities: Ameren's 2027-31 capital plan rose to $38.1bn with a 13.3% rate base CAGR and 8-10% EPS CAGR. TC Energy raised 2026 EBITDA guidance and extended its 5-7% EBITDA CAGR through 2031. Targa raised 2026 EBITDA guidance to at least $6.0bn. DTE's Vantage sale leaves 2027 guidance flat and JPM expects weakness.

Metals and mining: MP Materials 3Q adjusted EBITDA of $41M beat the pre-print Bloomberg consensus by about 50% on a one-off $32M SEG+ sale, and shares are down 30% over three months. Centrus reported 3Q revenue of $56M, about 3% above consensus.

market_movers.rationale: JPM would be buyers on weakness given the discounted valuation. The portfolio review ended with no incremental asset sales, so the stock reaction is expected to be modestly negative.

Downgraded from Overweight. Adjusted EBITDA of $38.2mm was 20% below JPM and revenue of $171mm was 24% below, with equipment awards and rig reactivations pushed into 2027.
Solid 3Q26 with record volumes and lower costs, but JPM sees a tighter product market and wider crude differentials favoring downstream and integrated models.
Lagged peers on higher beta to WTI and wider WCS discounts. JPM sees a relatively solid operational update.

Beat on a one-off SEG+ sale with qualification and ramp milestones on schedule. Shares are down 30% over three months and near valuation support, with headline risk from scrutiny of government support.
3Q results beat, FY28 targets were reaffirmed and no ATM shares were issued for a third straight quarter. YE27 price target is $45.
Record 3Q on energy storage and product sales, and guidance was raised. Dec 2027 target goes to $99 from $98.
3Q results matched the preannouncement. JPM withdrew its prior $5 target on lower sector trading multiples.
3Q beat and 2027 revenue guide above expectations. Target cut to $20 from $22 on a lower assigned multiple.
Bakken East cost range was tightened with the midpoint unchanged. Financing remains the open variable.
Oncor's 2027-31 capex plan is expected to rise about 20% to roughly $57bn. JPM sees 2026 EPS at the high end.

Vantage sale leaves 2027 guidance flat versus 2026. JPM expects weakness because the market punishes an EPS CAGR reset.
NY's Energy Affordability Index adds regulatory friction to rate requests. JPM sees a downward skew to outcomes with limited room for earnings upside.
Capital plan rose to $38.1bn with a 13.3% rate base CAGR and 8-10% EPS CAGR, and 2026 guidance was raised 10 cents.
4Q26 EBITDA outlook came in well above JPM and Street. JPM raised 2027E EBITDA by 11.6%.

sector_views.rationale: JPM sees a tighter product market and wider crude differentials, which favors downstream and integrated models over upstream Canadian producers.
The BTM, nuclear and IPP baskets are in a deep drawdown, with a median 50% fall from 52-week highs, as AI infrastructure names led the Nasdaq sell-off. The report gives no formal stance.
Capital plan upgrades at AEE, SO, SRE and TRP, and guidance raises at TRP and TRGP, support the growth outlook. DTE and ED are exceptions.

earnings_insights: EOG 3Q26 reported EPS $4.87 and CFPS $7.26, versus JPMe $4.53/$7.29 and Street (STe) $4.44/$7.06. Reported 11/5. 3Q26 EBITDAX $4.72bn, FCF $2.18bn, and 2026 FCF guidance of $9.7bn versus JPMe $8.9bn.
EOG 4Q26 guide: volumes 1.41 MMBoe/d (slightly below JPMe/STe due to ~16 MBoe/d of asset sales), oil 550 MBo/d, capex $1.68bn (2.5% above JPMe), and full-year capex ~$6.5bn reiterated.

DVN 3Q26 update reported 11/5. Portfolio review ended with no incremental asset sales beyond the $4.2bn Eagle Ford sale to Crescent (~$3.5bn after-tax). Committed to $1bn of 4Q26 buybacks. JPM expects a modestly negative reaction.
COP 3Q26 reported EPS $3.27 versus JPMe $3.15 and STe $3.09. CFPS $6.00 versus JPMe $5.88 and STe $5.78. FCF $4.0bn. Production 2.30 MMBoe/d. $2.4bn of buybacks versus JPMe $2.65bn.
HMH 3Q26 adjusted EBITDA $38.2mm versus JPMe $48mm, revenue $171mm versus JPMe $224mm, adjusted EBITDA margin 22.3% versus JPMe 21.2%, FCF -$11.6mm versus JPMe +$3mm, orders $191mm (+12% y/y).
TALO 3Q26 EBITDAX $406MM, about 5% above JPMe and 7% above STe. FCF $186MM versus JPMe $164MM and STe $143MM. FY26 guidance raised to 69 MBo/d and 93.5 MBoe/d.

Permian Resources 3Q26 cash flow beat by about 5%, with oil volumes about 2% above JPMe/STe. Completed $1.15bn of acquisitions, mostly Ridge Runner (~$1.025bn), and raised the FY oil guide to 202.5 MBo/d.
Tenaris 4Q26 implied EBITDA of $853mm versus JPMe $757mm and STe $753mm. JPM models 1Q27 EBITDA of $903mm versus a prior $806mm.
Pembina 3Q adjusted EBITDA $1,128mm versus JPMe $1,028mm and Street median $1,044mm. Lower end of 2026 guidance raised to $4.45-4.55bn.
TC Energy 3Q26 comparable EBITDA $3,004mm versus JPMe $2,928mm and Street median $2,893mm. 2026 guide raised to $11.8-12.0bn and 2027 guide set at $12.3-12.5bn.
Targa 3Q26 adjusted EBITDA $1,504mm versus JPMe $1,468mm and Street median $1,471mm. 2026 guidance raised to at least $6.0bn.

MP Materials 3Q adjusted EBITDA $41M versus pre-print Bloomberg consensus, a beat of about 50% driven by a $32M SEG+ sale. Centrus 3Q revenue $56M, about 3% above consensus, with backlog $7.0B versus $4.5B.
Ameren 3Q26 EPS was ahead of expectations and 2026 guidance was raised 10 cents. Ormat, HASI and Centuri beat on 3Q. Sempra and DUK beat on 3Q EPS. MDU missed 3Q and reaffirmed its 2026 EPS guide.

vol_and_positioning: CTAs likely turned net short US equities after momentum signals broke, with ~$11Bn of S&P 500 futures net selling in the first ~1.5 hours of cash trading.
Volatility-targeting portfolios have an estimated ~$50Bn of equity exposure to sell over the next few days as target leverage falls from the 67th to the 30th percentile.
Levered ETFs de-levered for the second time in a week, selling an estimated $60Bn+ of equity exposure into the close, ~90% in tech (semis, NDX, XLK).

geopolitical: Iran reported at least five tanker incidents near Hormuz since Sunday. Tehran said two tankers struck mines and one caught fire.
Ukrainian drones reportedly struck the area around Russia's Ryazan refinery (340 kb/d) ahead of next week's trilateral talks.
Iran sent a nuclear proposal to Washington via Qatar with seven demands (sanctions relief, unfrozen assets, reparations). Washington is reviewing it and no agreement exists.

US escalation options per JPM's Center for Geopolitics: a repeat of spring strikes, attacks on energy and civilian infrastructure, or a performative strike on a nuclear target. The MOU collapsed in June.
Trump said an Iran war decision is coming soon (Axios headline).
Democratic midterm gains raise scrutiny of Trump-backed critical minerals financing deals.
Lula's election win dashes US hopes of quick access to Brazil's rare earths (Reuters headline).
Qatar LNG-related OCTG shipments to the Gulf have not resumed, per Tenaris commentary.

tension_points.bull_case: A narrower Strait-focused arrangement is the best realistic near-term outcome. It would reduce economic and military pressure, and Iran's proposal via Qatar is under review.
tension_points.bear_case: The US and Iran remain far apart. Tanker incidents are rising and every US escalation option risks Iranian retaliation and higher energy prices.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A weekend that passes without escalation is the investors' 'all clear'. Escalation or a collapse of the Qatar channel would break it.

tension_points.bull_case: JPM would be buyers on weakness. The stock is discounted, buybacks are committed at $1bn in 4Q26 with a faster pace in 2027, and the Delaware Basin is getting more capital.
tension_points.bear_case: The portfolio review ended with no incremental asset sales, which disappointed investors who expected asset sales to fund aggressive buybacks.
